full_judgment: 13. Mr. Abul Kalam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate at the very outset raised the question of locus standi of the plaintiff of the original suit in filing the suit. Mr. Chowdhury submitted that after the repeal of Act No. I of 1969 by promulgation of PO No. 29 of 1972 the office of Assistant Custodian and Deputy Custodian was abolished. He submitted that the property which was declared as Enemy was vested with the Government and, as such, the plaintiff of the suit had no locus standi to institute the suit challenging the execution proceedings as well as the auction sale held in Money Execution Case No. 10 of 1973. Thereafter he submitted that the Money suit was instituted in 1962 and the suit was ultimately decreed in full by the High Court Division in Second Appeal No. 842 of 1964 and, as such, the decree in execution was made in a suit prior to the promulgation of Defence of Pakistan Ordinance and Rules and, as such, the legality and validity of the execution proceedings as well as attachment cannot be challenged by the Assistant custodian who had no authority to institute the suit. He submitted that the plaintiffs totally failed to prove the fact that Monoranjan left the country for India during the life time of Enemy Property Act and, as such, the Courts below were quite justified in dismissing the suit. He further submitted that the notices of Money Execution Case No. 10 of 1973 was duly and lawfully served upon Monoranjan and, as such, under section 114(e) of the Evidence Act there carries a presumption that the claim of vesting with the enemy property was baseless and, as such, the Courts below did not commit any illegality in dismissing the suit. With these submissions Mr. Chowdhury prayed for discharge of the rules.
